chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Yahya al-Azraq, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'I circumambulated four circuits and became tired, so can I pray its two cycles while seated?' He said, 'No.' I said, 'So how does a man pray the night prayer when he is ill and finds slackness, while seated, and this one cannot pray?' He said, 'Is it correct for you to perform Tawaf while you are seated?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'So pray while standing.'
ai.seo_question: Can I pray the two cycles of Tawaf while seated if I am tired?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of Salat al-Tawaf by establishing that the prayer must be performed while standing, even if the pilgrim is fatigued, drawing a direct analogy from the standing requirement of Tawaf itself. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on maintaining the physical posture of prayer (Qiyam) as a condition for validity in this specific act of worship, distinguishing it from general concessions for illness. The dialogue underscores the precision with which Imam al-Sadiq (AS) derived legal rulings from the physical mechanics of the ritual.
